claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a high-temperature single-phase BCC state.
The high-temperature BCC state of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has high configurational disorder.
Phase stability of high-temperature BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed primarily by configurational entropy.
At high temperature, configurational disorder lowers the free energy and stabilizes a single-phase state.
Above a critical temperature, configurational entropy dominates the phase stability of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
At moderate or lower temperatures, enthalpic effects can drive phase separation in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 when sufficient diffusion time is available.
The relevant structural mediator is the loss of atomic-scale configurational disorder through developing short-range chemical order.
Slow cooling permits diffusion-mediated local rearrangements that optimize enthalpic interactions.
Diffusion-mediated chemical ordering nucleates and grows secondary phases in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Rapid quenching kinetically suppresses diffusion-mediated ordering and preserves the high-temperature disordered state.
Slow-cooled Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 will transform toward a multiphase or chemically heterogeneous microstructure.
Rapidly quenched Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 will largely retain a single-phase BCC structure.
The proposed mechanism applies only when atomic mobility exceeds a minimum diffusion threshold.
A five-component oxide provides prior evidence that configurational entropy can drive a reversible transformation between multiphase and homogeneous single-phase states.
Indistinguishable single-phase BCC structures after slow cooling and rapid quenching would falsify the proposed ordering-driven transformation mechanism.
